title: a release callback that leaves its owner set, so the owner refuses the recursive forget and the handle is freed twice
live_proof: inspection of REL_17_5 contrib/pgcrypto/openssl.c: ResOwnerReleaseOSSLCipher at :799-803 hands the object to free_openssl_cipher with no `cipher->owner = NULL;` (2aa6be6e64 adds exactly that line), and free_openssl_cipher at :299-305 calls EVP_CIPHER_CTX_free(od->evp_ctx) and THEN `if (od->owner != NULL) ResourceOwnerForgetOSSLCipher(...)`. Real resowner.c at the same pin raises from ResourceOwnerForget when owner->releasing is set. Quoted in PROVENANCE.md
object: od->evp_ctx, the EVP_CIPHER_CTX from OpenSSL's allocator
lifetime_ender: the release callback frees the handle and then calls ResourceOwnerForget during release, which resowner.c refuses with an ERROR; abort cleanup releases the same item again and the handle is freed a second time
shape: double release through an item the owner never forgot
allocator_layer: libc (OpenSSL's allocator for the EVP handle); the OSSLCipher struct itself is aset and is NOT the object freed twice
nested_why: At the pin free_openssl_cipher frees the EVP handle BEFORE the ResourceOwnerForget that raises, so pfree(od) is never reached on either pass: od leaks, and the object freed twice is OpenSSL's. That is what makes this a temporal, NON-nested defect in the backend, and the counterexample to the idea that the backend is all nested.
fidelity: real subject, transcribed consumer: resowner.c and the memory managers are compiled unmodified from the pin and raise the error themselves; openssl.c's two functions are transcribed in shape with the EVP handle modelled by a libc allocation, because pgcrypto in place needs the px framework and OpenSSL
memory_error_is_the_defect_why: The defect IS the second EVP_CIPHER_CTX_free. The error that gets it there is raised by real resowner.c, not injected by the case.
fault_sites_why: the second free is the invalid operation, and it is made in one labelled frame so a fault can be attributed to the defect rather than to the sequence

native-detect.oracle: build-host.sh: the control must complete, then the defect run must either exit 0 having released one handle twice, or be killed with a host-allocator double-free diagnostic
native-detect.verdict_note: real resowner.c raised "ResourceOwnerForget called for pgcrypto OpenSSL cipher handle after release started", abort cleanup released the same item again, glibc: "free(): double free detected in tcache 2", SIGABRT exit 134; the control completed exit 0 and showed the error raised twice, which is upstream's error cleanup loop

host-asan.oracle: the same program under -fsanitize=address: ASan must report attempting double-free, with the report's frame in ro_free_probe
host-asan.verdict_note: AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free; #1 ro_free_probe shared/driver.c:57, #2 free_openssl_cipher case.c:57

status: built and reproduced on the host (native-detect, host-asan); no capability arm has been run
